boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Springfield record (January 8, 1863) in Marmaduke's First Expedition into Missouri [January 1863]. The capture of Fort Lawrence (Beaver Station) and Ozark (January 6-7) and the Confederate appearance on the Rolla road on January 9 are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Southwestern District of Missouri Troops (2,000) [US], and the frozen US bound is 2,000; the live field reads 2000 (US 2000; CS 0). Britton says Brown reported Marmaduke with five thousand men and a battery, that Burch's prisoners gave five or six thousand, that the garrison had been reduced to perhaps less than one thousand effective men, that about four hundred stragglers and convalescents were armed, and lists Brown's units with their numbers; nearly two hundred citizens also fought. Marmaduke says he struck with about 1,000 men under Shelby and 270 under MacDonald, and that the Federal force was 4,200.
claims.rationale: Intelligence estimates, a garrison figure before reinforcement, unit counts from a history and an interested claim of enemy strength. The frozen 2,000 has no inspected basis, and Britton's unit counts are not summed here. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live CS zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory, although the raid ultimately failed, and the live result Union Victory. Marmaduke says that at dark he held the greater part of the town, a fort and a captured gun, and did not renew the attack next day. Britton says the Confederates were driven back into the college palisades at dark and Marmaduke declined another action on the 9th. NPS says the depot was successfully defended.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The accounts differ on the ground held at dark.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 403 total (US 163; CS 240), as does the live field. Britton gives the Federal loss as 14 killed, 146 wounded and 4 missing, Marmaduke's reported loss as 20 killed and 124 wounded, and Crabb's report of 60 to 80 Confederate wounded left on the field. Marmaduke's January 18 dispatch gives 20 killed and 80 wounded; his February 1 report gives 33 killed, 203 wounded and 29 missing for the whole expedition. The No. 9 return for January 2-11 is garbled in OCR.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The expedition total covers Springfield, Hartville and the skirmishes and is not assigned to this record.

open_questions: Curtis's, Brown's, Holland's and Crabb's reports (Nos. 1-4), Shelby's and Bennett's reports (Nos. 10, 12) and a legible copy of the No. 9 return remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume I (Putnam's, second edition, revised, 1891) is a retrospective history whose title page says it is based upon the official reports of named Federal and Confederate commanders; its preface says the author served with the Federal army in that section and almost invariably took the official reports as a guide for numbers and casualties. It is not independent of the Official Records families and is treated as partly a participant's interested Union account. Marmaduke's January 18 and February 1, 1863 reports are one author family of interested Confederate accounts; Holmes's printed indorsement and the compiled No. 9 casualty return (garbled in OCR) are not counted as further families. Official Records Series I, Volume XXII, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
